title: autoformat workflow commit identity: take author from github.event.issue.user, map Bot authors to mlflow-app[bot] with fixed ID 191841109
answers: Autoformat commit shows the wrong author name or noreply email on a PR opened by a bot
Where does the autoformat workflow decide the git user.name and user.email for its commit?
Why does the autoformat job no longer call gh pr view or gh api to look up the PR author?
How do I change the noreply email format used for autoformat commits?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/autoformat.yml, job whose "Configure git" step runs on a slash-command comment (autoformat trigger) and sets git user.name and user.email before pushing the formatted commit to the PR branch.
Rule: The author identity is read from the workflow event payload (github.event.issue.user.login, .id, .type) passed to the step as AUTHOR_LOGIN, AUTHOR_ID, AUTHOR_TYPE. Do not call gh pr view or gh api users/<login> for it; those add token-scoped API calls. When AUTHOR_TYPE is "Bot", LOGIN is forced to "mlflow-app[bot]" and ID is the hardcoded 191841109, so the bot's ID must be updated in this step if the app changes. Email stays in the form ${ID}+${LOGIN}@users.noreply.github.com.
Symptom: Autoformat commits on bot-authored PRs were attributed to the wrong identity or needed extra API calls to resolve the author's numeric ID.
Constraints: Applies only to the autoformat workflow's git identity step. For human authors the ID comes straight from the event payload, so no lookup is needed. Other workflows that commit as a bot are not covered by this change.
applies: Autoformat workflow git identity (commit author name/email) for PRs whose author is a human or the mlflow-app bot.
says: Code formatting commits on bot pull requests show the wrong author name.
Automatic formatting commits are not attributed to the application bot profile.
Ensure format command commits use the correct noreply email for bot branches.
Triggering code formatting via pull request comments hits API rate limits.
Attribute automated code formatting commits directly to the pull request author.
search: The autoformat workflow (`.github/workflows/autoformat.yml`) derives git author identity directly from event payload fields rather than querying GitHub APIs. When `AUTHOR_TYPE` is `Bot`, `LOGIN` is forced to `mlflow-app[bot]` with ID `191841109`, constructing the email as `${ID}+${LOGIN}@users.noreply.github.com`. This rule applies exclusively to the git identity step of the autoformat workflow for human or bot PR authors and does not cover other workflows committing as a bot.
